presentingComplaint: Fever, confusion and a witnessed seizure over 3 days
history: Previously well 34-year-old man with a 3-day history of fever and frontal headache, followed by progressive behavioural change (uncharacteristic irritability, disorientation to time and place) and one witnessed generalised tonic-clonic seizure this morning. Partner reports word-finding difficulty and transient odd smells the day before. No recent travel, animal or tick exposure, no immunosuppression, fully immunised. No neck trauma or drug use.
examination: Febrile, GCS 13 (E3 V4 M6), disoriented with expressive dysphasia and a subtle right facial droop. Mild neck stiffness but no true meningism; Kernig negative. No papilloedema on fundoscopy. No rash, no lymphadenopathy, no ear/sinus focus. Cardiovascular and respiratory exam normal.
imaging: MRI brain with contrast: T2/FLAIR hyperintensity and swelling of the right medial temporal lobe and insular cortex with gyral restricted diffusion, sparing the basal ganglia - classic HSV encephalitis distribution. EEG: right temporal periodic lateralised epileptiform discharges (PLEDs).
microbiology: CSF HSV-1 DNA PCR positive; bacterial culture and Gram stain negative; CSF enterovirus and VZV PCR negative.
citations: Harrison 22e - Acute Meningitis and Encephalitis (Viral CNS Infections)
stewardship: Empiric IV aciclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours started immediately on clinical suspicion (before PCR result), because untreated HSV encephalitis carries high mortality and delay worsens outcome. Add empiric IV ceftriaxone (+/- ampicillin for Listeria cover if risk factors) until bacterial meningoencephalitis is excluded, then stop once CSF confirms HSV. Continue aciclovir 14-21 days; ensure adequate hydration and monitor renal function.
contraindications: Aciclovir nephrotoxicity - dose-adjust for renal impairment and hydrate to prevent crystal nephropathy
Avoid LP before imaging if focal deficit, GCS drop or suspected raised ICP (mass effect risk)
Beta-lactam allergy affects choice of adjunctive bacterial cover
edgeCases: Early MRI and even initial CSF HSV PCR can be negative in the first 72h - repeat PCR at 3-7 days and continue aciclovir if clinical suspicion remains high
Anti-NMDA-receptor autoimmune encephalitis can follow (post-HSV) or mimic viral encephalitis, especially with prominent psychiatric features and movement disorder
Lymphocytic CSF with mildly raised protein and normal glucose overlaps with TB and partially-treated bacterial meningitis
expectedMaiK: Fever plus encephalopathy, focal temporal-lobe signs, seizure and a lymphocytic CSF with positive HSV-1 PCR and medial temporal MRI changes indicate HSV encephalitis; empiric IV aciclovir must not wait for confirmatory testing as early treatment is the key determinant of survival and neurological outcome.

crossAccept.rationale: Encephalitis and bacterial meningitis sit on the meningoencephalitis spectrum with overlapping empiric cover (ceftriaxone±acyclovir), but are distinct - flag.

regressionAssertions: empiric therapy must include aciclovir (antiviral), not antibiotics alone
differential must include a bacterial CNS infection (MENINGITIS)
